_comment: Guided tour for the F-test / chi2-max calculator. Steps point at real controls and wait for the user. Read by chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: What this answers
steps.text: You fitted the same data with a simpler and a more complex model. The complex one has the lower χ² — it always does. The question is whether the drop is more than noise. Five steps.

steps.title: Load the fits, not the numbers
steps.text: From fit lists every open fit. Send the simpler one to model 1 and the more complex one to model 2; χ²r and ν = points − free parameters come across exactly.

await.hint: Press 📊 From fit and choose a fit for model 1, then again for model 2.

steps.title: Read the confidence
steps.text: F.cdf(χ²r₁/χ²r₂; n₁, n₂). Near 1: the extra parameters are justified. 0.5: no preference. This variance-ratio form is conservative for two fits of the same data — see the guide for the sharper extra-sum-of-squares test.

steps.title: Or ask what χ² you need
steps.text: Type a confidence here and the tool solves for the χ²r₂ the complex model must reach. It overwrites χ²(2).

steps.title: The threshold of one fit
steps.text: χ²max is the χ²r below which a parameter set is still inside the confidence region. Set params to 1 for the interval of a single parameter.

await.hint: Set params to 1 and press Enter; watch χ² max drop.

steps.title: Where the threshold comes out
steps.text: χ²min · (1 + p/ν · F(p, ν; conf)). The profile scan in the fit window stops at this level for a least-squares fit.
